drhp.business: MTNL provides wireline and wireless telecom services (landline, broadband, FTTH, leased line and 2G/3G mobile) in Delhi and Mumbai, running telephone exchanges in both cities. Under a Service Agreement signed with BSNL on 22.11.2024 and effective 01.01.2025, BSNL runs MTNL's telecom services completely, bears the CAPEX and OPEX for the operation, and migrated customers are billed and collected by BSNL, with MTNL recognising a revenue share. Per the Union Cabinet decision of 27.07.2022, MTNL is left with land/building assets which it continues to monetize to discharge its loan liabilities.
drhp.expansion: MTNL has no expansion programme of its own. Its existing network has become obsolete, and the report says heavy debt and recurring losses leave MTNL unable to invest in modernising, upgrading or expanding it. Under the DoT OM of 02.08.2022 and the Service Agreement with BSNL (signed 22.11.2024, effective 01.01.2025), BSNL runs MTNL's telecom operations in Delhi and Mumbai and provides any CAPEX they need; the CAPEX sits on BSNL's balance sheet. risks.note: The CBCRM post-paid wireless billing system, installed in 2005, is down in Mumbai (average bills are being sent) and runs in Delhi without AMC or support; the wireline billing system also runs without AMC or support until migration to BSNL platforms.

Many MTNL IT systems are declared critical information infrastructure and are exposed to hacking and spoofing. Cyber-security efforts are subject to financial constraints, and data breaches carry regulatory penalties.
risks.risk: Cyber security, critical information infrastructure and data privacy

- BSNL runs all of MTNL's telecom operations in Delhi and Mumbai and bills migrated customers, so MTNL's revenue comes as a share recognised from BSNL. Long-pending reconciliation of balances between the two is still before a joint committee.
- The statutory auditors reported a material weakness in the operating effectiveness of internal financial controls as at 31.03.2026. Balance confirmations, TDS and subscriber-receipt reconciliations and CWIP capitalisation are also incomplete, and all of these are audit qualifications.
- The CBCRM post-paid wireless billing system, installed in 2005, is down in Mumbai (average bills are being sent) and runs in Delhi without AMC or support; the wireline billing system also runs without AMC or support until migration to BSNL platforms.
- Hardware for CSMS, ISP, broadband, FTTH and CBCRM has reached end of support with no spares available; it will only be phased out as BSNL fully takes over the services.
- Many MTNL IT systems are declared critical information infrastructure and are exposed to hacking and spoofing. Cyber-security efforts are subject to financial constraints, and data breaches carry regulatory penalties.
- Software packages are linked through interfaces or manual steps that leave gaps between them. Management calls the risk of having no ERP inherent, and integration with BSNL's systems is still to be examined.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
